thread: EIR 00210772 — Great House Farm, Williams/Buckler family (request, clarification and response)
subject: Re: EIR/FOI request - 00210772 (Great House Farm / Church View Close, Llandough) – Further Clarification and Request for Full Disclosure
body:
FOI Unit / Evelyn Morgan / Information Governance Team,

Thank you for your email dated 2 June 2026 and for the assistance provided
so far in relation to reference 00210772.

I appreciate the Council's efforts to support this important family matter
and note your confirmation that no records are held regarding the private
legal proceedings in *BP Properties Ltd v Buckler*.

As background, this case related to the longstanding claims of my
Williams/Buckler family to ownership of Great House Farm (Ty Mawr). My
grandmother Mary Williams maintained until her conveniently timed death in
1983 (in the 2 week window to challenge BP's registration of our home and
land since 1667, in their names) that our family held ownership of the
house following arrangements with Daniel Thomas involving the quarry, with
the surrounding farmland subject to a lease that defaulted.

There was a conveyance for the surrounding land and attempt to merge our
farmhouse and garden into that single plot in 1975. Which was challenged by
my nan. Something HM Land Registry correspondence (titles WA231076 and
WA240304, first registered to BP Properties Limited in 1982/1983)
references these conveyances and the Court of Appeal decision, which may
assist in narrowing relevant planning and heritage searches.

To enable your Planning, Heritage, and other relevant teams to conduct
thorough searches without further delay, I confirm that enquiries should
cover the historic Great House Farm / Ty Mawr estate in Llandough (adjacent
to and including areas now known as Church View Close, north side of
Leckwith Road, title WA231076). This includes any planning permissions,
heritage assessments, demolition records (circa 1988), tenancy notations,
environmental information, or correspondence from 1875 onwards.

I am keen to receive a full and timely response within the statutory
timeframe, drawing on all information the Council holds across departments.
This is of profound personal and historic importance to the Williams family
descendants as we seek to document and substantiate our family's position.
Should any records have been transferred to Glamorgan Archives or handled
in any other way, details of this would be most helpful.

Thank you once again for your understanding and support in this sensitive
matter. I look forward to your substantive reply at the earliest
opportunity.

Kind regards,

*Sion Buckler Esq. (Ret'd Sergeant)* bpvsbuckler.datro.xyz 5 Robin Hill,
Dinas Powys CF64 4TF (On behalf of the Williams / Buckler family
descendants)

thread: FOI/EIR — Planning permission Church View Close (June 2026 request)
subject: Planning Permission Church View Close, Llandough
note: No separate acknowledgement or reference for this request appears in the mailbox; the Council's response of 7 July 2026 under 00210772 addresses the same subject.
body:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and, where applicable, the
Environmental Information Regulations 2004, I request copies of records
relating to Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough, near Cardiff.

I am specifically seeking:

1. Planning applications, permissions, refusals, conditions, appeals, and
related correspondence concerning the demolition of Great House Farm and
subsequent residential development.

2. Any archaeological assessments, surveys, reports, briefs, watching
briefs, excavation reports, or heritage impact assessments relating to the
site.

3. Any correspondence between the Council, Cadw, BP Properties, BP,
developers, archaeologists, the Royal Commission, or other public bodies
concerning:
- Great House Farm;
- its historic significance;
- archaeological discoveries;
- listing or scheduling considerations;
- demolition proposals.

4. Any records discussing reported Roman remains, medieval remains,
monastic remains, burials, architectural fragments, or other archaeological
features associated with the site.

5. Any records relating to emergency listing, spot-listing, preservation,
or protection measures considered for Great House Farm during the 1980s.

6. Any committee minutes, officer reports, recommendations, or briefing
papers relating to planning decisions affecting the site.

If some records are held in archives or under a different authority, please
advise where they may be located.

I would prefer the information in electronic format.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler

https://bpvsbuckler.datro.xyz

subject: Church View Close, Llandough
body:
Sirs/ Ma'am,

I'm piecing together something I experienced in Llandough in 1988. From
public record, my research and family testemony. And media.

This is ongoing but here's a video of where my mind at is so far. It's
looking very aweful. I just thought I'd share this to invite you to
comment/ advise on any of this case.

My family seem to have been murdered into silence. But have never
surrendered claim to land in Llandough. Our home, my home, since 1667.

I am trying to communicate this story and please understand its
challenging. There's trauma, anger/ upset and it's fragmented across family
and various historic govenrment archives. It's collosal and multi
generational too.

https://youtu.be/INfFOLndny0?feature=shared

Website below. I will work to get all these evidence onto this website so
there's a chrononical timeline and central location for the evidence.

This matter is unresolved in many ways and I feel it needs to be handled. I
feel it's unacceptable all this could have been allowed to have happened
and gone on and buried or ignored for decades.

For authority to be authority there in South Wales, there must be
legitimacy. Be legitimate about this is all I ask.

Regards,

Sion Buckler
bpvsbuckler.datro.xyz
